# UI Text and Localization Reference

The project does not currently have an i18n package or translation directory. Do not invent `useTranslation`, generated translation types, or a Nuxt i18n setup.

## Current Rule

- Keep user-visible text intentional and consistent with the dashboard language.
- Centralize repeated labels and status messages in a small typed constants module when duplication appears.
- Use `Intl.NumberFormat` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for locale-sensitive numbers and dates.
- Do not build labels by unsafe string concatenation when structured formatting is clearer.
- Include accessible names for icon-only controls.

## Future Localization

If localization becomes a requirement, choose one Next.js-compatible library first, define the locale strategy, and migrate text systematically. Do not add a partial translation abstraction for one component.

## Formatting Example

```ts
const usdFormatter = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
  style: "currency",
  currency: "USD",
  maximumFractionDigits: 0,
});

export function formatUsd(value: number): string {
  return usdFormatter.format(value);
}
```

Charts and accessible summaries must use the same formatting helpers so visual and textual values agree.
